After 5-6: bash scripts/test_all.sh contract again, plus for t in tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh; do bash "$t"; done.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
CXX       = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-g++
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
                    rt_c_hvm_data
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file vplat_gettimeofday \
                       vplat_window
# C++ vplat smoke fixture: static ctors/dtors + libstdc++ containers
# through the same two-flag link, with g++ instead of gcc.
RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_cpp

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.c $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.h \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \

                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

# Linux-ABI app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3+): -nostdlib, no
# andesim runtime at all -- vlinux is what sets these up, not crt0.S. Link
# base 0x10000, the roadmap's "App image" base; -e _start since there is no
# crt0 to fall into it via link order.
LINUX_APP_CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS := -nostdlib -static -Wl,-e,_start -Wl,-Ttext=0x10000

# Real static-glibc app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4+): the vendor
# Linux-ABI toolchain (separate from HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN's bare-metal newlib
# one), ordinary static link -- no -Ttext override, the toolchain's own
# default static-exec layout (non-PIE, link base ~0x50000) just works with
# vlinux's loader as-is. Deferred to use-time (recursive `=` + $(error)) so
# `make all` (which does not need LINUX_TOOLCHAIN) is unaffected.
linux_glibc_tc = $(if $(strip $(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)),$(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN),$(error LINUX_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
GLIBC_CC = $(linux_glibc_tc)/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     rt_linux_argv.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

rt_linux_argv.elf: rt_linux_argv.c
	$(CC) $(LINUX_APP_CFLAGS) $(LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS) $< -o $@

# NOT part of `all` -- needs the optional LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (env-gated, like
# the rv32 fixtures need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32). Build individually:
# make rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf
rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf: rt_linux_glibc_hello.c
	$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@

# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U5: File I/O syscall set. Same toolchain/link as
# rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf; NOT part of `all` for the same reason.
rt_linux_file.elf: rt_linux_file.c
	$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@

# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U6: Time syscalls. Same toolchain/link.
rt_linux_time.elf: rt_linux_time.c
	$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@

# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U7: File-backed private mmap. Same toolchain/link.
rt_linux_mmap.elf: rt_linux_mmap.c
	$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@

# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9: marker'd glibc kernel under hybrid. Same
# toolchain/link, plus the installed andesim/ROI.h include path (the same
# runtime/ build every vplat fixture uses via -B/-specs -- this fixture
# just needs the ONE header, not the whole bare-metal runtime).
rt_linux_matvec.elf: rt_linux_matvec.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall \
	  -I $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include $< -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
# the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# C++ smoke fixture: the g++ driver adds -lstdc++ -lm itself; everything
# else (crt0, crtbegin/crtend, andesim.ld, lib group) comes from the specs.
$(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.cpp $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CXX) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      rt_linux_argv.elf rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf rt_linux_file.elf \
	      rt_linux_time.elf rt_linux_mmap.elf rt_linux_matvec.elf \
	      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \
	      lm_drain.o lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_all.sh -- build the andesim artifacts. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim build` subcommand (which moved out of the driver
# binary). It only orchestrates the existing build scripts / Makefiles; the
# build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
#
# TARGET (default: all):
#   all       setup.sh (locate external qemu + vsim + plugin) then
#             fixtures (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib too)
#             then vlinux
#   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
#   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
#   runtime   build/runtime/ (rv64) + build/runtime/rv32/ (rv32, when
#             HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set): libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o,
#             andesim.ld, andesim.specs, include/andesim/ROI.h
#   vlinux    build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf (the vlinux proxy-kernel
#             skeleton, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md; depends on the runtime
#             lib, built automatically)
#
# --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
#
# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

TARGET=all
DRY_RUN=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    all|plugin|fixtures|runtime|vlinux) TARGET="$arg" ;;
    *)
      echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|plugin|fixtures|runtime|vlinux] [--dry-run]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

# run one step: print it under --dry-run, otherwise banner + execute (inheriting
# stdio so the user watches the build live). set -e aborts on the first failure.
run() {
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$*"
    return
  fi
  printf '[build_all] %s\n' "$*"
  "$@"
}

# plugin: build_qemu_plugin.sh wraps `make -C qemu_plugin`; plugins build against
# the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h (no QEMU source tree needed).
case "$TARGET" in
  all)      run bash "$ROOT/setup.sh"; run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures"; run make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" ;;
  plugin)   run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh" ;;
  fixtures) run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  runtime)  run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_runtime.sh" ;;
  vlinux)   run make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U2 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): `andesim run --mode fast --runtime
# linux app.elf -- <app argv>` stages a manifested vlinux.elf (this run's app
# path + mem-size stamped into its .manifest section via objcopy) and boots
# THAT under -bios, instead of the app ELF directly.
#
# Scope for U2: only --mode fast is wired (cycle/hybrid are rejected for now;
# hybrid wiring is ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9). App argv (-- ...) threads
# into the manifest as argv[1..] (U8) -- this dry-run test proves the
# objcopy step + manifest app-path AND argv round-trip, matching the
# roadmap's Input/Output contract.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$elf" ] || fail "no fixture ELF under tests/fixtures"

# 1. dry-run contract: objcopy step printed, -bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf,
#    engine-synced CPU, the 1G mem-size default, qemu itself stays a preview.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux --dry-run "$elf" \
      -- -m x.gguf -t 1 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "dry-run exit $rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'riscv64-unknown-elf-objcopy' \
  || fail "missing the objcopy step: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--update-section .manifest=' \

# F9 contract: `run --mode hybrid --trigger marker` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 ->
# vsim handoff (no QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure. This is
# the marker slice; pc triggers, --mem-size, and --verify land as the feature
# grows. Layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): hybrid_trigger (CLI -> Trigger) + the trigger->argv
#      mapping and state threading (plan-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, missing --trigger, an unknown trigger, an extra positional.
#   3. --dry-run builds the 2-step [qemu fast-leg -> vsim accurate-leg] plan
#      (a throwaway cycle-accurate engine resolves it; nothing is spawned).
#   4. real handoff (guarded, best-effort): until the shared ABI is pinned to the
#      external vsim the resume ABI-mismatches, so a real run is recorded, not
#      gated.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 marker cores)
for t in hybrid plan; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andesim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan)"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, every case errors before a spawn
# (expect: assert rc + output regex; shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)
expect 2 'missing ELF'          "$BIN" run --mode hybrid
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'trigger.*is required' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid "$ELF"
expect 2 'unknown trigger'      "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, extra positional, missing --trigger, unknown trigger"

# 3. --dry-run builds a 2-step plan. A throwaway cycle-accurate engine resolves
# the accurate leg without a real vsim build; nothing is spawned.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/v1" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
if [ "$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"vsim:v1","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","roles":["accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"accurate-leg":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'

echo "[ok] --dry-run: 2-command marker plan (qemu64 fast-leg -> vsim accurate-leg)"

# external vsim, the resume ABI-mismatches, so this is recorded, not gated.
QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
SIM=$(ls "$(vsim_bin_dir)"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)

  ID=$("$SIM" --describe 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's/.*"id"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' | head -1)
  out=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker ${ID:+--engine "$ID"} "$ELF" 2>&1); rc=$?

    echo "[ok] real marker handoff: cycle figure line produced (rc=$rc)"
  else
    echo "[skip] real marker handoff: no cycle figure line (rc=$rc) -- expected until the shared ABI is pinned to the external vsim"
  fi
else
  echo "[skip] real handoff: need built qemu+vsim+plugin"
fi

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env ("" when neither is set).
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F9 contract: `run --mode hybrid --trigger marker` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 ->
# vsim handoff (no QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure. This is
# the marker slice; pc triggers, --mem-size, and --verify land as the feature
# grows. Layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): hybrid_trigger (CLI -> Trigger) + the trigger->argv
#      mapping and state threading (plan-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, missing --trigger, an unknown trigger, an extra positional.
#   3. --dry-run builds the 2-step [qemu fast-leg -> vsim accurate-leg] plan
#      (a throwaway cycle-accurate engine resolves it; nothing is spawned).
#   4. real handoff (guarded, best-effort): until the shared ABI is pinned to the
#      external vsim the resume ABI-mismatches, so a real run is recorded, not
#      gated.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 marker cores)
for t in hybrid plan; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andesim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan)"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, every case errors before a spawn
# (expect: assert rc + output regex; shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)
expect 2 'missing ELF'          "$BIN" run --mode hybrid
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'trigger.*is required' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid "$ELF"
expect 2 'unknown trigger'      "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, extra positional, missing --trigger, unknown trigger"

# 3. --dry-run builds a 2-step plan. A throwaway cycle-accurate engine resolves
# the accurate leg without a real vsim build; nothing is spawned.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/v1" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
if [ "$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"vsim:v1","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","roles":["accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"accurate-leg":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
fi
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/v1"
out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "dry-run rc=$rc: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq 'dry-run: 2 command'        || fail "dry-run: no 2-command banner: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq 'fast-leg \[qemu64\]'       || fail "dry-run: no fast-leg step: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq 'accurate-leg \[vsim:v1\]'  || fail "dry-run: no accurate-leg step: $out"
echo "[ok] --dry-run: 2-command marker plan (qemu64 fast-leg -> vsim accurate-leg)"

# 4. real handoff (guarded + best-effort). Until the shared ABI is pinned to the
# external vsim, the resume ABI-mismatches, so this is recorded, not gated.
QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
SIM=$(ls "$(vsim_bin_dir)"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -n "$SIM" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ]; then
  ID=$("$SIM" --describe 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's/.*"id"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' | head -1)
  out=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker ${ID:+--engine "$ID"} "$ELF" 2>&1); rc=$?
  if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$'; then
    echo "[ok] real marker handoff: cycle figure line produced (rc=$rc)"
  else
    echo "[skip] real marker handoff: no cycle figure line (rc=$rc) -- expected until the shared ABI is pinned to the external vsim"
  fi
else
  echo "[skip] real handoff: need built qemu+vsim+plugin"
fi

ok "F9 run --mode hybrid --trigger marker"

# vsim handoff (no QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure. This is

# grows. Layers:

#      mapping and state threading (plan-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, missing --trigger, an unknown trigger, an extra positional.
#   3. --dry-run builds the 2-step [qemu fast-leg -> vsim accurate-leg] plan
#      (a throwaway cycle-accurate engine resolves it; nothing is spawned).
#   4. real handoff (guarded, best-effort): needs built qemu+vsim+plugin, so a
#      real run is recorded, not gated here; scripts/run_e2e.sh is where real
#      handoffs are hard-gated on every fixture.

ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc

# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/e2e.sh must print kernel_cycles -- the vsim mcycle delta over the
# measured region (vsim drain - QEMU1 drain, offset 624) -- for both
# trigger modes (marker, pc), so the `./andesim run --mode hybrid
# --trigger marker|pc` surface carries the cycle figure.
#
# Fixture: rt_c_v_matmul.elf (marked RVV GEMM). Marker mode uses the
# ROI marker HINTs in the source; PC mode resolves the boundaries
# from the binary itself (no planted _hybrid_*_pc labels).
#
# Manual TDD smoke test (runs real QEMU+vsim round-trips); not wired into
# scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)
FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/log.sh"
. "$ROOT/setup.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# Resolve the PC immediately after `jal vmatmul_kernel` in the marked
# GEMM ELF; that's the PC at which vsim drains for PC mode (ROI_END).
# Recompiling the fixture relocates this address, so we derive it from
# objdump every run.
resolve_post_jal_pc() {
  local elf="$1"
  "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump" -d "$elf" \
    | awk '
        /jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/ { matched = 1; next }
        matched { sub(":", "", $1); printf "0x%s\n", $1; exit }
      '
}

check_mode() {
  local mode="$1"; shift
  local out rc n
  out=$(env FIXTURE="$FIXTURE" TRIGGER_MODE="$mode" EXPECT_RC=0 TIMEOUT=120 \
        "$@" bash "$ROOT/tests/e2e.sh" 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 77 ]; then
    echo "[skip] $mode round-trip skipped (rc=77, e.g. toolchain missing)"
    return 0
  fi
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$out"; fail "$mode round-trip did not exit 0 (rc=$rc)"; }
  n=$(echo "$out" | sed -nE 's/.*kernel_cycles\][[:space:]]*([0-9]+).*/\1/p' | head -1)
  { [ -n "$n" ] && [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; } \
    || { echo "$out"; fail "$mode: kernel_cycles not a positive integer (got '${n:-}')"; }
  echo "[ok] $mode round-trip printed kernel_cycles=$n"
}

check_mode marker

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
  echo "[skip] pc round-trip: HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset (run \`source ./setup.sh\`)"
else
  POST_JAL_PC=$(resolve_post_jal_pc "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf")
  [ -n "$POST_JAL_PC" ] || fail "could not resolve post-jal PC for vmatmul_kernel"
  check_mode pc ROI_START=vmatmul_kernel ROI_END="$POST_JAL_PC"
fi

echo "PASS test_kernel_cycles"

# Shared status printers + config/path resolution for test scripts.
# Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#   cfg_val KEY            -> KEY's value from the repo-root config.env
#   vsim_bin_dir           -> external vsim build dir (env, then config.env)
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env ("" when neither is set).
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR
}

+# contract test). Fatal on build failure.
+# build_driver + point BIN at the driver binary. The caller keeps its own
+# [ -x "$BIN" ] assertion (the failure messages vary per script).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Andes-CSR capability parity (the flywheel / drift guard).
#
# The offline deriver (scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py) computes, from a
# core's config.inc, which Andes CSRs it implements. The vsim
# engine compiles the SAME gate logic (src/hybrid/andes_caps*.hpp) and reports
# the list at runtime via `--describe` ("andes_csrs"). Fed the engine's OWN
# embedded build config.inc, the two must be byte-identical -- a disagreement
# means the resume/drain capability gate is wrong for that engine.
#
# Runs against EVERY built engine under $VSIM_BIN_DIR (each sim_* binary with
# a V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc beside it) -- a single hardcoded engine left
# new engines with zero parity coverage. Uses the engine's build config.inc
# (the exact blob the binary embeds), so offline and online share one source.
# The --describe half is opportunistic: it needs the engine rebuilt with the
# S3 describe change (a prebuilt binary that omits "andes_csrs" is skipped).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

DERIVE="$ROOT/scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py"
[ -f "$DERIVE" ] || fail "missing deriver: $DERIVE"

VSIM_BIN_DIR="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/../vsim_andesim/build}"

checked=0
for ENG in "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_*; do
  [ -x "$ENG" ] || continue
  name=$(basename "$ENG")            # sim_<engine>
  engine=${name#sim_}
  # The engine's embedded config.inc (copied next to its Verilated objects).
  CFG="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V$engine/obj_sc/config.inc"
  [ -f "$CFG" ] || fail "$name present but its build config.inc not found at $CFG"

  offline=$(python3 "$DERIVE" "$CFG") || fail "deriver failed on $CFG"
  [ -n "$offline" ] || fail "deriver produced an empty list for $CFG"

  online=$("$ENG" --describe 2>/dev/null \
    | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(" ".join(json.load(sys.stdin).get("andes_csrs", [])))' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$online" ]; then
    echo "[skip] $name --describe has no andes_csrs (rebuild vsim with the S3 change)"
    continue
  fi

  [ "$online" = "$offline" ] || fail \
    "PARITY MISMATCH ($engine): --describe andes_csrs != offline deriver"$'\n'"  describe: $online"$'\n'"  offline:  $offline"
  echo "[ok] $engine: --describe == offline deriver"
  checked=$((checked + 1))
done

[ "$checked" -gt 0 ] || { echo "[skip] no built engines under $VSIM_BIN_DIR"; ok "andes caps parity (skipped)"; exit 0; }
ok "flywheel: --describe == offline deriver on $checked engine(s)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F1 contract: QEMU plugin exits with code 200 on drain (matches vsim's
# kExitHandoffToQemu). 0 is reserved for "workload completed normally".
# The orchestrator (F2+) uses this distinction to decide the next spawn.
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_ELF     a CSR-trigger fixture (default: handoff_roundtrip.elf)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-handoff_roundtrip}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-plugin-drain-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU" >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[plugin_drain_exit_code]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
  echo "--- qemu log ---"
  cat "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[plugin_drain_exit_code]: state file is empty"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[plugin_drain_exit_code] PASS: QEMU exit=$RC, state size=$(wc -c <"$STATE_QEMU") bytes"

  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
      exit 77
    fi
  done
}

# Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
# $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
# absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
hybrid_describe_int() {
  "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
}

# Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
# the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
put_word_le() {
  local v=$3 bytes="" i
  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
  done
  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
}

6	# (resume at vaddr+size), but a pc boundary is real user code: if the plugin
7	# reports vaddr+size, the boundary insn executes on NEITHER leg (e.g. a
8	# skipped vsetivli leaves vtype.vill set and the vsim window faults on the
9	# first vector op). The plugin must report the boundary's own vaddr so the
10	# insn runs inside the measured window.

13	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
14	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so

18

26	command -v "${NM:-nm}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || NM=nm
27	ENTER_HEX=$("$NM" "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '$3 == "main" { print $1; exit }')
28	[ -n "$ENTER_HEX" ] || { echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: no main in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }

3	# and drains that as write_mask[] under HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK. The wm_drain

61	    int mxstatus = hybrid_wm_test(s.write_mask, HYBRID_WM_ANDES_BASE + HYBRID_WM_ANDES_IDX_mxstatus);
62	    int mcache   = hybrid_wm_test(s.write_mask, HYBRID_WM_MCACHE_CTL);
63	    int mmisc    = hybrid_wm_test(s.write_mask, HYBRID_WM_MMISC_CTL);
64	    int ucode    = hybrid_wm_test(s.write_mask, HYBRID_WM_ANDES_BASE + HYBRID_WM_ANDES_IDX_ucode);
65	    if (!mxstatus) { fprintf(stderr, "mxstatus bit clear (csrw not tracked)\n"); return 6; }
66	    if (!mcache)   { fprintf(stderr, "mcache_ctl bit clear (csrw not tracked)\n"); return 7; }
67	    if (mmisc)     { fprintf(stderr, "mmisc_ctl bit SET (csrr wrongly counted as write)\n"); return 8; }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# v5 contract: QEMU seeds the L2C Control Register (0xE0500008) with its DS220
# 11.8.7 reset value CEN=1 (L2 enabled by default). A fixture that NEVER writes
# the register (handoff_roundtrip) must still drain CEN=1 -- proving a guest that
# relies on the reset default is not silently handed a disabled L2 (CEN=0).
#
# Required environment (auto-detected):
#   VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF (FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-handoff_roundtrip}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

REPO_ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-plugin-l2c-rst-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
CHECK_SRC=$(mktemp --suffix=.c)
CHECK_BIN=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG" "$CHECK_SRC" "$CHECK_BIN"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU" >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[plugin_l2c_reset_default]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
  cat "$QEMU_LOG"; exit 1
fi

cat > "$CHECK_SRC" <<'EOF'
#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
#include <stdio.h>
int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    FILE *f = fopen(argv[1], "rb");
    if (!f) return 2;
    struct hybrid_state_v1 s;
    if (fread(&s, 1, sizeof(s), f) != sizeof(s)) return 3;
    fclose(f);
    if (!(s.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_L2C)) { fprintf(stderr, "HYBRID_FLAG_L2C not set\n"); return 5; }
    unsigned long long ctrl = (unsigned long long) s.l2c.reg[HYBRID_L2C_OFF_CONTROL / 8];
    if ((ctrl & 0x1u) != 0x1u) { fprintf(stderr, "CEN not set: l2c.ctrl=0x%llx\n", ctrl); return 6; }
    printf("OK: reset default CEN=1, l2c.ctrl=0x%llx\n", ctrl);
    return 0;
}
EOF
cc -std=c11 -I "$REPO_ROOT/include" "$CHECK_SRC" -o "$CHECK_BIN"

if "$CHECK_BIN" "$STATE_QEMU"; then
  echo "PASS[plugin_l2c_reset_default]"
else
  echo "FAIL[plugin_l2c_reset_default]: L2C reset default CEN=1 not observed"
  exit 1
fi

input.new_string:
# Spawn QEMU for a plugin-only drain test: boot $VSIM_ELF on andes_ae350 with
# the hybrid plugin attached, stdin detached, combined output to LOG.
#   plugin_qemu_drain LOG PLUGIN_ARGS [EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS...]
# PLUGIN_ARGS is the plugin argument string after "$VSIM_PLUGIN," (e.g.
# "outfile=$STATE"). Sets RC to QEMU's exit code -- deliberately not local,
# callers gate on it -- and toggles errexit off around the spawn exactly like
# every call site used to. No shared-memory backend: plugin-only tests have
# no vsim leg, so nothing else ever opens the mmap, and the machine's default
# RAM is the same 128 MiB the backend used to force.
plugin_qemu_drain() {
  local log="$1" plugin_args="$2"; shift 2
  set +e
  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -machine andes_ae350 \
    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    "$@" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$plugin_args" </dev/null >"$log" 2>&1
  RC=$?
  set -e
}
